reason: The v1 geometry/depth-only freeze found only two eligible targets under a one-target-per-reference-scan rule and opened zero RGB members. V2 changes only the pre-RGB diversity constraint; the 32-pixel visibility contract, target-triple exclusions, model, score and decision gate remain unchanged.

overrides.question: Does the frozen 3D Street View center-scale lock retrieve three distinct stable 3RScan doors or doorframes across registered rescans when geometry supplies fully visible proposals and at most two targets may come from one reference scan?

frozen_cohort.selection_order: Use candidate_protocol rows in its frozen descending area_proxy order. Exclude every exact consumed target triple; require a unique physical (reference_scan_id, target_instance_id) within this cohort; permit at most two selected targets per reference_scan_id; select the first three rows whose reference and rescan both pass the unchanged frame_rules. Pose, depth and instance geometry may be read during freeze; RGB members must remain unopened until replay.

overrides.claim_boundary: A pass is a small real-image Development canary that the frozen same-point appearance lock transfers from outdoor 3D Street View to truth-proposed stable indoor 3RScan door or doorframe instances. 3RScan mesh, pose, depth, RGB and semantic labels come from one provider; target triples are disjoint from the four enumerated prior cohorts, but up to two targets may share one reference scan and scan families may have appeared in prior Development; proposals use privileged reconstructed geometry; and only three physical targets are tested. It is not door detection, pixel-mask transfer, doorway aperture, named entrance, venue ownership, public access, traversability, approach waypoint, arrival, HANDOFF_READY, open-world or provider-independent confirmation, user benefit or mobility-safety evidence.
